paper.title: The Emergence of Firms in a Population of Agents: Local Increasing Returns, Unstable Nash Equilibria, and Power Law Size Distributions
paper.journal: CSED Working Paper No. 3, Brookings Institution / Santa Fe Institute; see also Axtell (2001), Science 293:1818

headline: Axtell 1999/2001 Model of Firms (agent-based): 1/3 locked clauses REPRO; Zipf rank-size slope=-1.277 (base mu~1.28), firm-size Gini=0.474, log-growth excess kurtosis=0.590 with sigma-vs-size slope=-0.078

verdicts.gate: P1 Zipf firm sizes: rank-size log-log OLS slope in [-1.5, -0.7]
P2 extreme inequality: firm-size Gini >= 0.60 (strongly right-skewed)
reasons: mean firm-size Gini = 0.4743 over 4 seeds (range [0.458, 0.488]); need >= 0.6. The distribution IS strongly right-skewed (mean firm size 2.67, max 83, 1872 firms), but this faithful base case (A=5000, nu=2, equal shares) concentrates less than the empirical ~0.89

verdicts.gate: P3 tent-shaped log-growth: pooled excess kurtosis > 1.5 AND sigma falls with size
reasons: mean growth excess kurtosis = 0.5895 over 4 seeds (range [0.471, 0.697]); need > 1.5. Sign IS correct (leptokurtic, heavier-than-Gaussian tails) and sigma-vs-size slope = -0.0781 < 0 (Stanley scaling holds directionally), but the peak is not Laplace-strength (~3) in this base case

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic agent-based model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + locked-prediction discipline reproduce the Zipf firm-size power law, extreme size inequality, and tent-shaped growth from endogenous firm formation, and would catch an artifact

citations: Axtell, R. (1999). The Emergence of Firms in a Population of Agents: Local Increasing Returns, Unstable Nash Equilibria, and Power Law Size Distributions. CSED Working Paper No. 3, Brookings Institution / SFI.
Axtell, R. (2001). Zipf Distribution of U.S. Firm Sizes. Science 293:1818. doi:10.1126/science.1062081.
Stanley, M.H.R. et al. (1996). Scaling behaviour in the growth of companies. Nature 379:804-806. doi:10.1038/379804a0.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the Zipf rank-size slope, the firm-size Gini, and the log-growth excess kurtosis + sigma-vs-size (Stanley) slope
